newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to miss deficit goal, join EMU-Kuehbacher.
newsitem.headline: Germany to miss deficit goal, join EMU-Kuehbacher.

text.p: Germany will fail to cut its budget deficit this year to the Maastricht Treaty goal of three percent of GDP, but should still be allowed to join European monetary union in 1999, a central banker said on Tuesday.

"Germany will not achieve the deficit criterion in 1997," Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said here. He added: "We don't necessarily have to interpret three percent new borrowing as three-point-zero percent...Germany should be there from the beginning."

Kuehbacher also said a delay to EMU would be worse than allowing certain convergence criteria in the Maastricht Treaty to be interpreted broadly. A delay would threaten to make EMU as a whole fail, he said.
The remarks by Kuehbacher, who is also president of the Berlin central bank, followed comments he made on Monday in which he cast doubt on EMU starting punctually.

He told the Berliner Zeitung newspaper he was not sure EMU would start on time because the German government was unlikely to meet the fiscal criteria without taking further steps to raise taxes or slash social spending.
